title: Flower Atlas Image Credits
text: Flower Atlas Image Credits The reference photos in the bouquet review ("Looks like") come from the platform's flower atlas. We use only images we may use commercially, and we credit every one of them. Where the images come from Wikimedia Commons — files under CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA. The credit follows Commons’ suggested form: Author, licence, via Wikimedia Commons, with a link to the file page. iNaturalist — research-grade observations whose photos are CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA. The credit is the photo’s own attribution, via iNaturalist, with a link to the photo. Our own photos, and photos from partner florists or growers given to us with written permission. We never use Google Images or any other source without a clear licence, and never images under non-commercial (NC) or no-derivatives (ND) licences. Every image is checked by our team before any florist sees it. The current list The live list of every published image, with its author, licence and source link, is public: in the Vendor Portal: Image credits in the page footer (/Atlas/Attributions, no sign-in needed); as data: GET https://api.findmyflowers.pl/api/v1/atlas/attributions. In the review, hover over a “Looks like” picture to see its credit, or click it to open the source page. Licences Licence What it allows What we must do CC0 1.0 Any use Nothing (we still name the source) CC BY 4.0 (and older versions) Any use, including commercial Credit the author, link the licence, say if we changed the image (we resize it) CC BY-SA 4.0 (and older versions) Any use, including commercial As CC BY; our resized copy is shared under the same licence Found a problem with an image or its credit? Write to contact@findmyflowers.pl and we’ll fix or remove it.

title: Auth Flows
text: # Authentication & Authorisation Flows ## Keycloak OIDC Login (Production) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client as Mobile App / Portal participant KC as Keycloak (dev :8090; prod auth.findmyflowers.pl) participant API as REST API participant MW as TenantResolutionMiddleware participant Redis as Redis (Blacklist) Client->>KC: POST /realms/flowershop/protocol/openid-connect/token Note over Client,KC: grant_type=password or PKCE code exchange KC-->>Client: access_token (JWT), refresh_token Client->>API: GET /api/v1/... Authorization: Bearer {token} API->>Redis: TokenBlacklistMiddleware.IsRevoked(jti)? Redis-->>API: false API->>KC: Validate token signature (JWKS) KC-->>API: Valid API->>MW: TenantResolutionMiddleware MW->>MW: Extract claims: sub, role, vendor_id, vendor_type, customer_id MW->>MW: ITenantContextService.Set[Vendor|Customer|Admin]Context() MW-->>API: Tenant context set API-->>Client: 200 OK note over Client,Redis: Error path: token revoked → 401 Unauthorized note over Client,Redis: Error path: tenant claims missing → 403 Forbidden ``` > **Google SSO (EP-23):** the `flowershop` Keycloak realm has a `google` identity provider. On a customer's first Google login, `CustomerProvisioningService` performs just-in-time provisioning — creating the `Customer` aggregate and linking it to the Keycloak user — after which the standard OIDC flow above applies. ## Dev Token (Development Only) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Dev as Developer participant API as REST API (Authentication__UseKeycloak=false) Dev->>API: POST /api/v1/auth/dev-token {role, vendorId, customerId} API->>API: Generate JWT locally (no Keycloak) API-->>Dev: access_token (JWT with claims) Dev->>API: Any endpoint with Bearer token API->>API: TenantResolutionMiddleware reads local JWT claims API-->>Dev: 200 OK ``` ## Logout + Token Blacklist ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant API participant Redis as Redis (Blacklist) participant KC as Keycloak Client->>API: POST /api/v1/auth/logout Authorization: Bearer {token} API->>Redis: RedisTokenBlacklistService.RevokeAsync(jti, expiry) API-->>Client: 204 No Content note over API,Redis: Keycloak session is not terminated — only the JWT token is blacklisted Client->>API: GET /api/v1/... (same token) API->>Redis: IsRevoked(jti)? Redis-->>API: true API-->>Client: 401 Unauthorized ``` ## Multi-Tenant Context Resolution ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Request arrives] --> B[TokenBlacklistMiddleware] B -->|jti revoked| Z1[401 Unauthorized] B -->|valid| C[TenantResolutionMiddleware] C --> D{role claim?} D -->|VendorAdmin| E[SetTenantContext vendor_id + vendor_type + user_id] D -->|User| F[No vendor claims — falls through to header fallback or 403] D -->|PlatformAdmin| G[SetPlatformAdminContext user_id] D -->|missing| Z2[403 Forbidden] E --> H[TenantValidationBehavior in MediatR pipeline] F --> H G --> H H --> I[Handler receives ITenantContextService.GetTenantContext] ```

title: Payment Flows
text: # Payment Flows ## Full Stripe Checkout Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App as Mobile App participant API as REST API participant DB as PostgreSQL participant Stripe participant Outbox as EfOutboxWriter participant Dispatcher as OutboxDispatcherService participant Bus as InMemoryEventBus participant Hub as BouquetHub (SignalR) App->>API: POST /api/v1/orders {deliveryAddress} API->>DB: Create Order (status=PendingPayment) API->>DB: Reserve bouquets (status=Reserved, reservedUntil=now+15min) API->>Stripe: StripeService.CreatePaymentIntentAsync(amount, currency) Stripe-->>API: {paymentIntentId, clientSecret} API->>DB: Order.StripePaymentIntentId = paymentIntentId API-->>App: 201 {orderId, clientSecret} App->>Stripe: confirmCardPayment(clientSecret) Stripe-->>App: Payment result alt Payment succeeded Stripe->>API: POST /api/stripe/webhook (payment_intent.succeeded) API->>API: Verify webhook signature (Stripe-Signature header) API->>DB: Order status → Confirmed, bouquets → Sold API->>Outbox: EfOutboxWriter.Write(OrderPaidEvent) API->>DB: SaveChangesAsync (order + outbox in one transaction) Dispatcher->>DB: Poll OutboxMessages (every 5s) Dispatcher->>Bus: InMemoryEventBus.PublishAsync(OrderPaidEvent) Bus->>Hub: BouquetHub.SendAsync("OrderStatusChanged", orderId, status) Hub-->>App: Real-time notification else Payment declined Stripe->>API: POST /api/stripe/webhook (payment_intent.payment_failed) API->>DB: Order status → PaymentFailed API->>DB: Release bouquet reservations (status → Available) API-->>App: Real-time: payment-failed end note over DB,Stripe: Reservation auto-expires after 15min via OrderReservationExpiryService ``` > **Stripe is live.** `StripeService` (Stripe.net + Polly retries) is wired into `CreateOrderCommandHandler` and handles payment intents, webhook signature verification, refunds, and reconciliation. `StubStripeService` is only a dev fallback used when `Stripe:SecretKey` is not configured; production sets `Stripe:SecretKey` and `Stripe:WebhookSecret`. ## Order Cancellation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App as Mobile App participant API as REST API participant DB as PostgreSQL participant Stripe App->>API: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel API->>DB: Verify order status is PendingPayment or Confirmed (not Delivered) API->>DB: Order status → Cancelled API->>DB: Release bouquet reservations (status → Available) alt Has Stripe payment intent API->>Stripe: CancelPaymentIntent or Refund end API-->>App: 200 OK ```

# Concurrency View Describes the concurrent and parallel execution units in the system: processes, threads, background services, async I/O, and the coordination mechanisms used to prevent race conditions. ## Process & Thread Model The entire platform runs in a single ASP.NET Core process hosted by Kestrel. HTTP and WebSocket connections share the Kestrel thread pool; each request flows asynchronously through the MediatR pipeline. Roughly eight `IHostedService` background services run on the same process concurrently — `OutboxDispatcherService` (domain event delivery), `VaseHealthMonitoringService` (IoT liveness), `OrderReservationExpiryService` (release expired bouquet holds), `StripeWebhookProcessorService`, `PaymentReconciliationService`, `BouquetFreshnessUpdateService`, `PerformanceAnalyticsService`, and `SubscriptionMatchingService` — plus the MQTT startup subscriber for IoT message ingestion. # Information View Describes how the system stores, manages, and flows information. Covers data structure, ownership, lifecycle, and the key transformations data undergoes. ## Aggregate Ownership & Tenancy Every aggregate in the system belongs to exactly one ownership scope, which determines how it is isolated and queried. # Operational View Describes how the system is operated, monitored, and maintained once deployed. Covers health checking, error handling, configuration management, and known operational gaps. ## System Health Checks In dev, Docker Compose polls each service's dedicated health check. In production the platform runs as Fly.io apps (region `fra`) fronted by Cloudflare — Fly's health checks poll each app. The API's `/health` endpoint is the top-level signal for the application layer. Each infrastructure service exposes its own probe — PostgreSQL via `pg_isready`, Redis via `redis-cli ping`, MQTT via a broker probe (dev: Mosquitto `mosquitto_sub`; prod: HiveMQ Cloud, TLS 8883), and Keycloak via its `/health/ready` endpoint. All must report healthy for the platform to be considered fully operational; a failure in any one of them will block dependent service startup. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph HealthChecks["Health Check Endpoints"] HC["GET /health

(postgres-dev)"] RH["redis-cli ping
(redis-dev)"] MQH["mosquitto_sub -t $$SYS/broker/uptime
(mqtt-dev)"] KCH["curl /health/ready
(keycloak-dev)"] end ORCH["Health Poller
(Docker Compose in dev / Fly.io in prod)"] -->|polls| HC ORCH --> PGH ORCH --> RH ORCH --> MQH ORCH --> KCH ``` ### Sub-domain Mapping — Health Checks | Health Check | Business Sub-domain | What breaks if it fails | |-------------|--------------------|----| | `GET /health` (API) | All sub-domains | Entire API unavailable — no bouquet discovery, orders, or vendor management | | `pg_isready` (PostgreSQL) | All sub-domains | No persistence; all commands and queries fail immediately | | `redis-cli ping` (Redis) | **Identity & Tenancy, Customer Purchasing, Payments** | Token blacklist, idempotency, and query cache all unavailable; duplicate orders possible | | `mosquitto_sub` (MQTT) | **IoT / MQTT** | Vase telemetry (heartbeats, sensor data) not ingested; freshness scores stale | | `/health/ready` (Keycloak) | **Identity & Tenancy** | Vendor and customer login fails; dev-token mode unaffected | ## Request Error Handling Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart TD REQ["Incoming HTTP Request"] --> GEX["GlobalExceptionMiddleware

text: # Docs portal — `docs.findmyflowers.pl` behind sign-in (EP-38) `FlowerShop.DocsPortal` (ASP.NET Core 8, Fly app `flowershop-docs-portal`) serves the Jekyll build of `docs/` to signed-in readers only, per audience: | Docs role | Reads | Granted by (Keycloak) | |---|---|---| | `developer` | everything | realm role `PlatformAdmin`, group `developers` | | `vendor` | Vendor Portal + vendor mobile app manuals | realm role `VendorAdmin` | | `customer` | Customer app manual | realm role `User` (every registered customer) | Pages are **developer-only unless labelled** (`audience:` front matter or `defaults` in `docs/_config.yml`). The build emits `access-manifest.json` (path → audiences) and `search-{developer,vendor,customer}.json`; the portal never serves those files, removes navigation the reader can't open (`data-audience` in `_layouts/default.html` / `_data/nav.yml`) and answers `/search.json` with the union of the reader's indexes. ## How sign-in works - **Direct**: a visitor without a session goes to `/signin` → Keycloak (code + PKCE, client `flowershop-docs`). Google sign-in works for customers through the EP-23 identity provider; an existing Keycloak session (Customer App) signs in silently. `/signout` ends both sessions (RP-initiated logout). - **Help links from the apps** (Vendor Portal `Help`, Customer App `Help`, vendor app EP-M18): the app calls `POST /api/v1/docs/handoff` with its current access token and opens the returned URL. The docs portal redeems the 60 s single-use code back-channel with its own client credentials (`POST /api/v1/docs/handoff/redeem`), creates its session and continues to the page. Any failure falls back to the direct sign-in, then the same page. - **Session**: cookie `__Host-docs` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax), sliding 8 h, absolute 24 h (handoff sessions 8 h). Roles are re-read every 15 minutes (`POST /api/v1/docs/roles` → Keycloak admin API), so removing `VendorAdmin` or the `developers` group takes effect within 15 minutes. title: Rollback & Recovery Playbook
text: # Rollback & Recovery Playbook > **Purpose**: bring the platform back to a known-good state when a deploy goes wrong, a dependency falls over, or data gets corrupted. > **Principle**: rollback is always faster than root-cause analysis. Restore service first, investigate on a branch. ## Decision tree (60-second read) ``` Something is wrong in prod ├── Just deployed? → §1 Revert the deploy ├── Data plane (DB/Redis/Mq/Mqtt) offline? → §2 Dependency outage ├── One subdomain broken, others fine? → §3 Per-component recovery ├── Auth broken (nobody can log in)? → §4 Keycloak recovery ├── Data corrupted / bad migration? → §5 Database restore └── Whole site unreachable, DNS level? → §6 DNS & TLS emergency ``` --- ## §1 Revert the most recent deploy Each component has an independent release stream — revert only the one that broke. ### 1.1 Fly apps (`flower-shop-backend-core`, `flowershop-keycloak`, and the three portals) ```bash # List releases (newest first). fly releases --app flower-shop-backend-core # Roll back to previous. fly releases rollback --app flower-shop-backend-core # interactive — picks N-1 # or explicit: fly image show --app flower-shop-backend-core # get current image sha fly releases --app flower-shop-backend-core | head -5 # find the one before fly deploy --app flower-shop-backend-core --image registry.fly.io/flower-shop-backend-core: ``` Fly performs a rolling deploy; the old machine is drained cleanly. Expected downtime: 0. ### 1.2 Portal Fly apps (`flowershop-admin-portal`, `flowershop-vendor-portal`, `flowershop-customer-app`) Same as §1.1 — the portals are Fly apps too: ```bash fly releases rollback --app flowershop-admin-portal fly releases rollback --app flowershop-vendor-portal fly releases rollback --app flowershop-customer-app ``` Or simpler: re-run the previous green GitHub Actions run from the Actions UI — "Re-run all jobs". ### 1.3 Git-level revert (if the deploy shipped but the code is the problem) ```bash # Revert the bad commit — this is a PR, not a force-push. git revert git push origin main # The path-filtered workflow redeploys only affected components. ``` **Never** `git push --force` to `main`. Always prefer `git revert`. --- ## §2 Dependency outage (the SaaS vendor is down) | Dependency | How to detect | Immediate action | |---|---|---| | **Fly Postgres** | `/health/ready` shows DB `Unhealthy`; `psql` hangs | `fly status --app flower-shop-postgres`; `fly machines restart --app flower-shop-postgres` if a machine is stuck. If regional outage, wait it out — site goes read-mostly. See §5.2 for read-only fallback. | | **Redis** | not applicable in prod | Redis isn't provisioned; `RedisCacheService` falls back to in-memory. | | **RabbitMQ** | not applicable in prod | RabbitMQ isn't provisioned; `InMemoryEventBus` is the active impl. | | **HiveMQ** | MQTT health check fails; no vase heartbeats in logs | Restart API subscriber: `fly machines restart --app flower-shop-backend-core`. text: # Twilio Verify — operator setup (EP-29) Real SMS codes for customer phone verification (`POST /api/v1/profile/phone/send-code`). Until this is done, production answers **503 `sms-not-configured`** and the Customer App shows "Phone verification is temporarily unavailable" — it never pretends a code was sent. > Twilio's console menus get renamed from time to time. If a step's menu path is not where this > page says, type the feature name ("Geo permissions", "Verify Services") into the Console search. ## 1. Create the account (free trial) 1. Go to and sign up (email or Google). No credit card needed. 2. Verify your email, then verify **your own mobile number** by SMS — it becomes the first *verified caller ID*. 3. Onboarding questions: product **Verify**, use case **2FA / phone verification**, language **C#**. Trial limits: Verify can only send to **verified caller IDs** (up to 5 recipients), messages may carry a "Sent from a Twilio trial account" prefix. Add test phones under **Phone Numbers → Manage → Verified Caller IDs**. Upgrade the account before real customers verify. ## 2. Create the Verify service 1. **Verify → Services → Create new**. Friendly name `FindMyFlowers` (it appears in the SMS text). 2. Channels: enable **SMS** only. Code length **6** (the UI expects 6 digits). 3. Copy the **Service SID** (`VA…`). 4. In the service settings make sure **Fraud Guard** is enabled (blocks known SMS-pumping patterns). ## 3. Restrict destinations — Geo Permissions **Verify → Settings → Geo permissions** (or Messaging → Settings → Geo permissions): allow **Poland (+48)** only; disable every other country. This mirrors the in-app allow-list `Sms:Limits:AllowedCountryPrefixes` (default `["+48"]`) — keep both in sync when expanding. ## 4. Credentials → Fly secrets Copy **Account SID** (`AC…`) and **Auth Token** from Console → Account Info, then: ```bash fly secrets set -a flower-shop-backend-core \ Sms__Provider=Twilio \ Sms__Twilio__AccountSid=AC... \ Sms__Twilio__AuthToken=... \ Sms__Twilio__VerifyServiceSid=VA... ``` Set all four in one command (rolling restart). `Provider=Twilio` with any blank credential makes the API throw when the SMS service is first resolved. ## 5. title: Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option E (Freshness Visibility)
text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option E (Freshness Visibility) > Companion to EPICS.md (EP-01–09), EPICS-B.md (EP-10–18), EPICS-C.md (EP-19–22/23) and > EPICS-D.md (EP-24, Showcase Deployment). > Epic is numbered EP-25 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep25-bouquet-freshness-visibility.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-07-15 --- ## EP-25: Bouquet Freshness Visibility **Priority**: P2-medium **Dependencies**: EP-03 (bouquet discovery / map card), EP-13 (Customer Web App map) **Requirement refs**: REQ-FRESHVIS-01 through REQ-FRESHVIS-03 **State**: done > Vendors declare how long a bouquet stays fresh; customers see it on the map at a glance. ### Concept A vendor picks a **freshness rating of 1–3 flowers** when publishing a bouquet, where the number is the count of days the bouquet is guaranteed to stay fresh (`1` = up to one day, `3` = three days for sure). Customers see the rating on the map bouquet card as **three flower pictograms** — coloured flowers for the current level and greyed flowers for the remainder. A rating of `2` renders as two coloured flowers and one grey. The rating **decays by one flower per full day** since the bouquet was created: a bouquet published at rating `3` shows 3 coloured flowers on day 0, 2 on day 1, 1 on day 2, and 0 (all grey) from day 3. The decay is computed at read time from the creation timestamp — there is no background job and no stored countdown. ### Explicitly NOT part of this epic - **No price impact.** Setting or decaying the freshness rating never changes the price. Freshness-based *discounting* is a separate, pre-existing feature (`BouquetFreshnessUpdateService` + `FreshnessPricingStrategy`, configured per vendor). The two are intentionally decoupled — this epic is display-only. - **Not the sensor score.** `Bouquet.FreshnessScore` (0–100, sensor/MQTT-derived, `<20` ⇒ expired) is a different field and is left untouched. The vendor rating lives on the new `Bouquet.InitialFreshnessDays`. ### Domain model | Member | Meaning | |---|---| | `Bouquet.MaxFreshnessScale` (const = 3) | Number of pictograms the rating is shown against. | | `Bouquet.InitialFreshnessDays` (int?, 1–3) | Vendor-declared rating captured at creation; `null` when unset. | | `Bouquet.SetInitialFreshnessDays(int)` | Sets/updates the rating (clamped 1–3; `≤0` clears it). Never touches price. | | `Bouquet.CurrentFreshnessDays(DateTime utcNow)` | Decayed level = `Initial − fullDaysElapsed`, floored at 0; `null` when unset. | ### Stories & tasks See `docs/tasks/tasks-ep25-bouquet-freshness-visibility.json` (S-25-01; T-25-001 … T-25-005) for the authoritative breakdown. Summary: 1. **T-25-001** — `InitialFreshnessDays` + decay computation on the Bouquet aggregate (+ unit tests). 2. **T-25-002** — persistence: migration `AddBouquetInitialFreshnessDays` + snapshot. 3. **T-25-003** — expose `currentFreshnessDays` / `maxFreshnessScale` / `initialFreshnessDays` on read models and populate every bouquet query/command...

text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option F (Customer Portal Mobile Redesign) > Companion to EPICS.md (EP-01–09), EPICS-B.md (EP-10–18), EPICS-C.md (EP-19–23), > EPICS-D.md (EP-24) and EPICS-E.md (EP-25). > Epic is numbered EP-26 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep26-customer-portal-mobile-redesign.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-F.md` (REQ-CXUI-01 … REQ-CXUI-13). > Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-customer-portal-mobile-redesign-design.md`. > Mockups: `docs/assets/customer-portal-redesign/`. > Analysis date: 2026-07-18 --- ## EP-26: Customer Portal Mobile Redesign **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-13/EP-14 (Customer Web App), EP-08 (real-time markers), EP-16 (E2E Playwright), EP-18 (card/BLIK checkout), EP-25 (freshness pictograms) **Requirement refs**: REQ-CXUI-01 through REQ-CXUI-13 **State**: in-progress — design system, bottom nav and map redesign implemented; content pages restyled via the shared CSS; `dotnet build` + EP-16 Playwright re-run pending a .NET environment (T-26-013). > Give the customer portal a professional, Airbnb-style mobile experience without changing any > behaviour, contract or data. ### Concept The `FlowerShop.CustomerApp` works but looks dated on mobile — a large opaque filter card hides most of the map, the palette clashes (blue header + green button + grey body), and it reads as default Bootstrap. This epic restyles the whole customer portal to a **map-first, app-like** design in the spirit of Airbnb: a floating **search pill**, horizontal **filter chips**, white **price-pill** markers, a draggable **filter bottom sheet**, a **floating bouquet card**, and one consistent card/typography **design system** with a **bottom tab bar** across every screen. It is deliberately **presentation-only**: no API, DTO, handler, migration, auth or routing change. Every existing form field, JS handler, SignalR real-time hook (EP-08) and E2E `data-testid` (EP-16) is preserved. ### Design decisions - **Scope**: the full customer portal (map, details, cart, checkout, favourites, orders, profile) — it only reads as one app if every screen shares the system. - **Accent**: a single **rose `#E5326E`** replaces the blue+green mix. text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option H (AI Florist) > Companion to EPICS.md (EP-01–09), EPICS-B.md (EP-10–18), EPICS-C.md (EP-19–23), > EPICS-D.md (EP-24), EPICS-E.md (EP-25), EPICS-F.md (EP-26) and EPICS-G.md (EP-27). > Epic is numbered EP-28 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep28-ai-bouquet-assistant.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-H.md` (REQ-AIB-01 … REQ-AIB-19). > Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-ai-bouquet-assistant-design.md`. > Mobile counterpart: vendor app repo, EP-M10 (`docs/tasks/tasks-ep-m10-ai-bouquet-assistant.json`). > Analysis date: 2026-10-14 --- ## EP-28: AI Florist **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-02 (vendor auth / tenant context), EP-15 (R2 storage pattern), EP-24 (Fly.io deployment); vendor mobile app EP-M10 for the UI **Requirement refs**: REQ-AIB-01 through REQ-AIB-19 **State**: in-progress — backend implemented and tested (pilot prototype on free providers); Fly changes, provider evaluation and pilot rollout remain. > Stock first. Recipes first. Preview on demand. ### Concept A florist photographs what is on the bench (or types it in), corrects the estimated counts, picks a style and an optional cost ceiling, and gets up to three bouquet recipes that are guaranteed to fit the confirmed stock, each with an honest cost (missing prices are shown as missing, never as zero). An illustrative image is generated only when the florist taps *Generate preview* for one recipe. ``` Photos/manual ─▶ Recognition job ─▶ Estimated stock ─▶ Florist confirms ─▶ Composition job (billable) (billable) │ Save / share ◀── Recipe detail (cost, margin) ◀── Validated recipes (≤3) ◀───┘ │ └─▶ Preview job (billable, on demand, cached) ─▶ private image ``` ### Design decisions - **Code is the gatekeeper**: every proposed recipe (LLM or rule-based) is re-validated against the confirmed stock snapshot; invalid ones are dropped, never "repaired" with another paid call. - **Durable jobs in PostgreSQL**, not the RabbitMQ stub or the outbox: `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claims, renewable leases, no transaction across provider calls. - **The job row is the spend reservation and the idempotency record** — one table instead of three, with quota checks serialized by an advisory lock. - **No blind retries**: a post-submission loss is `OutcomeUnknown` (spend kept reserved); BFL's polling URL is persisted so a crash resumes polling instead of paying twice. - **Private media**: separate private R2 bucket, authenticated byte endpoints, EXIF stripped. - **Free by default**: `Fake` recogniser, rule-based composer and SkiaSharp placeholder previews let the whole flow be tested in the app before any paid provider is chosen. - **Worker in the API process for the pilot** — the API Fly machine must stay awake. ### Explicitly NOT part of this epic - Board screen 06 "Additions · later release" (supplier items, shopping list). - S/L sizes, flowerbox, recipe templates/regeneration history, hand-off to saleable...

Two migrations (`AddPhoneVerificationAttempts`, `UniqueVerifiedCustomerPhone`). Real SMS delivery switches on when the operator completes `docs/deployment/TWILIO-VERIFY-SETUP.md`; until then production answers an honest 503 "temporarily unavailable". > Make "verify your phone" safe to expose to the Internet: a normal customer verifies one number > with one code; a bot farm hits a wall long before it costs real money. ### Concept The phone-verification feature works, but production quietly runs the `Null` placeholder (fake "code sent", public magic code `123456`). Switching to Twilio Verify turns every "Send code" click into a paid SMS, which makes the endpoint a target for **SMS pumping** (toll fraud) and for **mass fake-account verification**. The defence is layered — each layer is cheap for a real user: | Layer | Stops | Normal user notices | |---|---|---| | Honest provider in prod | Fake success, magic-code bypass | Nothing (or a clear "unavailable") | | Real client IP + registration throttle | One host minting hundreds of accounts | Nothing | | Country allow-list (+ Twilio Geo Permissions) | Pumping to premium foreign ranges | Nothing (PL customers) | | ≤ 2 numbers / account / 30 days | One account spraying many numbers | Nothing | | Per-account & per-number daily caps | Many accounts hammering one number | Nothing | | Global daily budget | Any attack's worst-case bill | Only during an attack | | One verified number per account | Re-using one SIM for many accounts | Nothing | | Verified email + Turnstile | Scripted accounts reaching the SMS step | Invisible captcha | ### Design decisions - **Ledger, not counters in cache**: every send-code is a `PhoneVerificationAttempt` row. text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option J (Stock management) > Companion to EPICS.md (EP-01–09), EPICS-B.md (EP-10–18), EPICS-C.md (EP-19–23), > EPICS-D.md (EP-24), EPICS-E.md (EP-25), EPICS-F.md (EP-26), EPICS-G.md (EP-27), > EPICS-H.md (EP-28) and EPICS-I.md (EP-29). Epic is numbered EP-30 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep30-stock-management.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-J.md` (REQ-STOCK-01 … REQ-STOCK-11). > Mobile counterpart: vendor app repo, EP-M11 (`docs/tasks/tasks-ep-m11-stock.json`). > Analysis date: 2026-10-18 --- ## EP-30: Stock management **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-02 (vendor auth / tenant context), EP-12 (Vendor Portal), EP-28 (assistant — shares the catalogue key and consumes stock prices); vendor mobile app EP-M11 for the app UI **Requirement refs**: REQ-STOCK-01 through REQ-STOCK-11 **State**: in progress — backend, Vendor Portal and vendor app (EP-M11) implemented and tested; deployment (T-30-014) remains. > One stock per shop. Every change leaves a line in the ledger. ### Concept The assistant's stock is a throw-away snapshot of what is on the bench. EP-30 adds the shop's **running stock**: items (flowers, greenery, materials) with quantity on hand, unit cost and a low-stock threshold, changed only through movements — *received*, *used*, *wasted*, *counted* — so the history explains every number. ``` Delivery ──Received──▶ ┌────────────┐ ──Used──▶ bouquets (manual, or "deduct recipe" from the assistant) │ StockItem │ ──Wasted─▶ bin Stock-take ─Counted──▶ └────────────┘ │ unit cost ▼ AI Florist fills missing prices ``` ### Design decisions - **Counter + ledger**: `StockItem.Quantity` is the fast read; each change appends a `StockMovement` (delta, quantity after) in the same `SaveChanges`. The item row version serializes concurrent movements, so the ledger always adds up. - **Same catalogue key as the assistant** (`name|colour`, trimmed, lower-case) — unique per vendor — so stock, assistant sessions and recipe deduction match without ids. - **Whole units** like the assistant; flowers and greenery in stems. - **Replay-safe**: movements accept `Idempotency-Key`, stored on the ledger row with a filtered unique index, on top of the response-cache `IdempotencyMiddleware`. - **All-or-nothing batch consume** for recipes: no half-deducted bouquets. - **Archive, never delete**: history stays; the key stays reserved and can be restored. - **Independent of `BouquetDesign:Enabled`**: Stock works when the assistant is switched off. ### Explicitly NOT part of this epic - Lots/expiry/FIFO valuation, supplier purchase orders, shopping lists, auto re-order. - Automatic deduction on saleable bouquet creation or sale; low-stock push notifications. ### Stories & tasks See `docs/tasks/tasks-ep30-stock-management.json` (S-30-01 … S-30-06; T-30-001 … T-30-014). 1. **S-30-01 — Trackers and contracts** — T-30-001 docs · T-30-002 API + outbound contracts. 2. **S-30-02 — Domain** — T-30...

text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option K (Stock photos & AI appearance) > Companion to EPICS-J.md (EP-30 Stock management) and EPICS-H.md (EP-28 AI Florist). > Epic is numbered EP-31 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep31-stock-photos-ai-appearance.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-K.md` (REQ-STKPH-01 … REQ-STKPH-13). > Mobile counterpart: vendor app repo, EP-M12 (`docs/tasks/tasks-ep-m12-stock-photos.json`). > Analysis date: 2026-10-18 --- ## EP-31: Stock photos & AI appearance recognition **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-30 (stock), EP-28 (private media store, image processing, provider plumbing, usage gate and $ cap); vendor app EP-M12 for the app UI **Requirement refs**: REQ-STKPH-01 through REQ-STKPH-13 **State**: in progress — implemented and tested in both repos (backend, Vendor Portal, vendor app EP-M12); deploy (T-31-015) open. > A colour word is a guess. A photo is the truth; the AI turns it into words the florist confirms. ### Concept ``` Photo ──upload──▶ private store ──describe (AI, quota)──▶ suggestion ──florist applies──▶ appearance │ variety + colour label + palette swatches + pattern + description ◀──────────────────────┘ │ ├──▶ assistant composer: real shades for recipes ├──▶ assistant previews: stock photos as reference images └──▶ assistant recognition: bench photos matched to stock items ``` ### Design decisions - **Variety joins the identity**: key = name|colour[|variety]; items without a variety keep their existing key, so EP-30 data needs no key migration. - **Suggest, never overwrite**: AI output is a suggestion; only an explicit apply writes it, and the appearance records `source = Ai`. - **Synchronous describe with a ledger**: one photo, one short call. A ledger row is the reservation (inserted under the assistant's advisory lock), so quota and the shared $ cap stay exact; an `Idempotency-Key` replay returns the stored suggestion. - **Free by default**: the `Palette` provider measures dominant colours with SkiaSharp — real swatches with no AI spend; `OpenAI` adds variety/name and a richer description. - **Same private storage as the assistant** (`stock/{vendorId}/…` keys), same image pipeline. - **Backwards-compatible updates**: `variety`/`appearance` omitted from a PUT are left untouched. ### Stories & tasks See `docs/tasks/tasks-ep31-stock-photos-ai-appearance.json` (S-31-01 … S-31-07; T-31-001 … T-31-015). 1. **S-31-01 — Trackers and contracts** — T-31-001 docs · T-31-002 contracts. 2. **S-31-02 — Variety and appearance** — T-31-003 domain · T-31-004 commands/API. 3. **S-31-03 — Item photos** — T-31-005 entity/migration/storage · T-31-006 endpoints, pending photos, retention. 4. **S-31-04 — AI appearance recognition** — T-31-007 ledger/quota · T-31-008 providers · T-31-009 tests. 5. **S-31-05 — Assistant integration** — T-31-010 stock-linked lines · T-31-011 previews + composition · T-31-012 bench matching. 6. **S-31-06 — Vendor Portal UI** — T-31-013. 7. **...

After this epic, every rating, refinement > and stock correction makes the next answer for that shop better. title: Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option Q (Online-only vendors: bouquets without a smart vase)
text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option Q (Online-only vendors: bouquets without a smart vase) > Companion to EPICS.md (EP-03 discovery, EP-04 orders), EPICS-C.md (EP-19 onboarding, EP-21/22 > vases) and EPICS-O.md (EP-37 custom orders). > Epic is numbered EP-39 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep39-online-only-vendors.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-Q.md` (REQ-ONL-01 … REQ-ONL-19). > Mobile counterparts: vendor app EP-M19 (T-39-020); customer mobile app (T-39-021). > Analysis date: 2026-10-23 --- ## EP-39: Online-only vendors — sell bouquets without a smart vase **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-03 (discovery), EP-04 (orders + Stripe), EP-19 (registration), EP-20 (platform access) **Requirement refs**: REQ-ONL-01 through REQ-ONL-19 **State**: in progress — backend, Vendor/Admin Portal and Customer App implemented (S-39-02…05, S-39-07, T-39-019); vendor app EP-M19 (T-39-020) and the customer mobile app (T-39-021) are follow-ups in their repos. REQ-GAPS-Q §H decided as proposed (no Hybrid mode, no studio pickup, one listing = one sale, platform delivery radius). > The vase stops in-store and online customers buying the same bouquet. Online-only shops and > freelance florists never have walk-in customers or collections, so they don't need one. They list > a finished bouquet with a photo, it appears on the map as "Delivery only", and it sells once. ### Concept ``` Vendor.SalesMode = OnlineOnly Vendor Portal "Add a bouquet" ─▶ POST /api/v1/vendor/online-listings (photo, price, freshness) ─▶ Bouquet.ListOnline(...) ListingChannel = Online, VaseId = null, Status = Available ─▶ BouquetBecameAvailable ─▶ BouquetHub push + customer bouquet alerts Customer map (purchasable only, within delivery range, "Delivery only", fuzzed pin) ─▶ cart: IsPurchasable → Reserve (optimistic concurrency: one winner, others 409) ─▶ checkout: Delivery required (pickup-not-offered) → Stripe → vendor fulfils → Delivered → Sold Expiry: declared freshness reaches 0 or MaxListingDays elapsed → Expired (off the map) Vase-only side effects (MQTT, vase state) skipped by the existing VaseId != null guards ``` ### Design decisions - **No virtual vase.** A fake `SmartVase` would be hidden by the 30 s offline map filter. It would open EP-22 recovery incidents, receive MQTT commands, hold only one bouquet at a time and skew fleet and analytics counts. Every one of those needs an `IsVirtual` check in IoT code. A vase-optional listing touches far less: two guards, two columns and three null reads. - **Say what the bouquet is.** `ListingChannel` (Vase | Online) on the bouquet and `SalesMode` (InStore | OnlineOnly) on the vendor make the business rule explicit and checkable: `IsPurchasable`. "Has a vase" is no longer a stand-in for "can be sold". - **The bouquet status is the lock.** With no physical display, the lock is `Available → Reserved → Sold`, protected by the `Version` concurrency token. text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option R (Recognition confidence from human feedback) > Companion to EPICS-H.md (EP-28 recognition), EPICS-M.md (EP-33 feedback loop) and EPICS-N.md > (EP-34 stock count, EP-35 bouquet analysis, EP-36 cost assessor). > Epic is numbered EP-40 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep40-recognition-confidence-feedback.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-R.md` (REQ-CNF-01 … REQ-CNF-16). > Mobile counterpart: vendor app EP-M20 (T-40-016). > Related: EP-41 (`EPICS-S.md`) adds the flower atlas, item crops and image matching; it shares `FlowerTypeKey` (T-40-003). > Analysis date: 2026-10-23 --- ## EP-40: Recognition confidence from human feedback **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-33 (corrections, quality dashboard), EP-34/35/36 (the three reviews) **Requirement refs**: REQ-CNF-01 through REQ-CNF-16 **State**: in progress — implemented in this repo (S-40-01…05, S-40-07; T-40-001…015, 017, 018); vendor app EP-M20 (T-40-016) pending. §H decided 2026-10-23 as proposed: sharing is opt-out (on by default), "right" means the flower type matches, no shared image crops, starting thresholds in `BouquetDesign:Confidence:*`. Scores ship switched off (`ScoresEnabled: false`, see Rollout); the operator runs the backfill once after deploy. > "90 % sure" today is the model rating itself, and it says that about almost everything. After this > epic, the number means "florists checked answers like this N times and it was right X % of the > time". It is computed in code from florists' verdicts, and it tells the florist which lines to check. ### Concept ``` review line ── ✓ Right · ✗ Wrong (it's actually …/not in the bouquet) · ? ── count kept/edited │ explicit verdict (weight 1) confirm without touching → implicit verdict (0.25) ▼ RecognitionVerdicts (vendor-scoped) ──hourly──▶ platform cells (model, prompt, task, flower type, raw bucket; │ anonymous, used only with ≥ 3 vendors, per-vendor cap) └──on write──▶ shop cells (vendor, model, task, flower type) ▼ score = shop rate shrunk toward platform type rate shrunk toward model bucket prior (Beta-Binomial, decay) ▼ { identity, count } × { score, band High/Medium/Low, basis shop|platform|model|none, checks } ▼ portal: "Usually right · 41 checks" / "Check this" / "Often wrong" / "Not enough checks yet" code: StockMatcher multiplier · no auto-link when Low · stock count NeedsCheck · wider cost range ``` ### Design decisions - **Platform counts plus a shop adjustment** (decided 2026-10-23). One shop's verdicts alone are too few per flower type to be reliable. Anonymous counts are pooled across vendors, with no vendor id, text, photos or prices, and a cell is used only when at least 3 vendors contributed to it. Each shop's own verdicts then pull the score toward what that shop sees. This relaxes EP-33's "no cross-vendor learning" for counts only. text: # Epics, Stories & Tasks — Option S (Flower atlas, item crops and image matching) > Companion to EPICS-N.md (EP-35 bouquet analysis, EP-36 cost assessor), EPICS-K.md (EP-31 stock > photos) and EPICS-R.md (EP-40 recognition confidence from human feedback). > Epic is numbered EP-41 to continue the sequence. > Task tracker (ground truth): `docs/tasks/tasks-ep41-flower-atlas-image-matching.json`. > Requirements: `docs/tasks/REQ-GAPS-S.md` (REQ-ATL-01 … REQ-ATL-16). > Mobile counterpart: vendor app EP-M21 (T-41-018). > Analysis date: 2026-10-23 --- ## EP-41: Flower atlas, item crops and image matching **Priority**: P1-high **Dependencies**: EP-35/36 (analysis review), EP-31 (stock photos), EP-40 (`FlowerTypeKey`, verdicts) **Requirement refs**: REQ-ATL-01 through REQ-ATL-16 **State**: in progress — Phase 1 (S-41-02, S-41-03) and Phase 2 (S-41-04) implemented with tests, contract and docs (S-41-06 except the vendor app); Phase 3 (S-41-05) and vendor app EP-M21 (T-41-018) pending. REQ-GAPS-S §H decided 2026-10-24 as proposed (open sources + own/pilot photos, no shared atlas from vendor crops, in-process ONNX, PL + EN). > Each line in the bouquet review shows three pictures: what the AI saw in your photo, what that > flower looks like, and the stock item it was matched to. Later, the pictures themselves are > compared, so the platform can say "the AI says astilbe, but this looks like amaranthus". ### Concept ``` photo(s) ─▶ LLM lists items + boxes {photoIndex, x, y, w, h} (bouquet-analysis-v2) │ └─ Phase 3, only if needed: open-vocabulary detector gives better boxes ▼ Skia crop (private, purged with the session) ├─ Phase 1 ─▶ atlas lookup by FlowerTypeKey + variety ─▶ licensed reference image + credit └─ Phase 2 ─▶ image fingerprint (CLIP/SigLIP, pgvector) ├─▶ nearest atlas photos → "photo looks like …" disagreement flag └─▶ nearest own stock photos → image factor in StockMatcher review line: [In your photo] [Looks like] [Your stock] + "Could be: Seeded eucalyptus" ``` ### Design decisions - **Combine, don't replace.** The LLM keeps listing and counting. Images confirm the identity and show the florist what the AI meant. Image fingerprints can't count overlapping stems and are weak on fine colour, so counts stay with the LLM and EP-40 feedback, and colour with the code's ΔE. - **Licensed atlas only.** No Google Images. Images come from Wikimedia Commons and iNaturalist (CC0/CC-BY/CC-BY-SA, with credit) and our own photos. Each one is reviewed in the Admin Portal before any vendor sees it. Credits are shown on hover and on a public attributions page. - **Two atlases.** The global atlas tells the florist what the flower is. The shop's own EP-31 stock photos act as a private atlas that says "you have this". The second one is where most of the value is, because it matches the bouquet to the shop's stock from the images, not from the AI's wording. - **Private by default.** Crops and vendor image vectors are vendor-scoped and purged with the session. text: # Requirement Gaps — Option I (Phone verification abuse protection) > Companion to REQ-GAPS.md (Mobile API), REQ-GAPS-B.md (Portals/Analytics/IoT), > REQ-GAPS-C.md (Vendor onboarding/subscription/vase), REQ-GAPS-D.md (Showcase deployment), > REQ-GAPS-F.md (Customer portal mobile redesign), REQ-GAPS-G.md (Contact us) and REQ-GAPS-H.md (AI Florist). > Requirement refs point at the tasks in `tasks-ep29-phone-verification-abuse-protection.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-10-16 > Status: all 13 requirements implemented (EP-29 done — see `EPICS-I.md`). ## Context Customer phone verification (EP-07 follow-up, `POST /api/v1/profile/phone/send-code` + `/verify-code`) is about to be switched from the `NullSmsVerificationService` placeholder to the real Twilio Verify provider on the public site `findmyflowers.pl`. Investigation on 2026-10-16 found: - **Production silently uses the placeholder.** `Sms:Provider` defaults to `Null`, no Fly secret sets it, and `NullSmsVerificationService` reports success without sending — so customers see "Verification code sent" but nothing arrives — and accepts the public magic code `123456`, so anybody can mark any number as verified. - **No cost/abuse controls.** The only guard is a per-user 5-requests/10-minutes rate limit shared by send and verify. There is no limit per destination number, per country, per account over time, nor a global budget. Every SMS costs money (Twilio Verify ≈ $0.05 + carrier fee), so the endpoint is an **SMS pumping (toll-fraud)** target: bots trigger sends to premium/attacker-controlled numbers. - **Fake accounts are free.** `POST /api/v1/customers/register` is anonymous and not rate-limited; behind Fly's proxy `HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress` is the proxy, so any per-IP limit would bucket all users together. - **A verified number is not unique.** Hundreds of accounts can each "verify" the same number. Goal: limit one account to 1–2 numbers, make mass fake-account verification uneconomic, and cap the worst-case SMS bill — **without adding friction for a normal customer** (one number, one or two codes, an invisible captcha). --- ## REQ-SMSABUSE-01 — No fake success in production — P0 When no real SMS provider is configured in the `Production` environment, `send-code` must fail honestly (`sms-not-configured`, HTTP 503) instead of pretending to send, and the magic code `123456` must never verify. text: # Requirement Gaps — Option M (AI Florist feedback loop & smarter wizard) > Companion to REQ-GAPS-H.md (AI Florist, EP-28), REQ-GAPS-K.md (Stock photos & AI appearance, EP-31) > and REQ-GAPS-L.md (AI Florist wizard in the Vendor Portal, EP-32). > Requirement refs point at the tasks in `tasks-ep33-ai-florist-feedback-loop.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-10-19 > Status: REQ-FBK-01 … 16 implemented in the API and Vendor/Admin Portals (EP-33, see `EPICS-M.md`); vendor app parity (EP-M13) pending. ## Context The AI Florist is open-loop today. The prompts are `const` strings in `Infrastructure/BouquetDesign/Providers/HostedAiProviders.cs` (`inventory-v1`, `recipe-v1`, `preview-v1`) and the model never hears how its last answer went. Specifically: - The vendor's only free-text input is `Style` (≤ 60 chars, `DesignLimits.MaxStyleLength`); size is fixed to M and the mode to AvailableOnly. - There are no ratings, refinement or per-vendor preferences. "Saved" (`SetSaved`) is a bookmark only. - Recipes the model gets wrong (`RecipeValidator` / cost ceiling) are dropped silently ("Only N of M recipes fit…"); the model never sees the reasons and is never asked to repair them. - Corrections the vendor makes to recognised stock (step 2) are lost; the next recognition repeats the same mistakes. - Provider evaluation (`docs/deployment/AI-BOUQUET-ASSISTANT.md` §5.4) is manual: florists rate results in a CSV kept outside the repo. `DesignJob` already stamps `Provider`, `Model`, `PromptVersion` and `LatencyMs`, so the signals this epic adds can be tied to the exact prompt and model that produced each result. **Principles kept from EP-28** 1. Nothing the model says is trusted: every recipe, including refined and repaired ones, goes through `RecipeValidator` and the cost-ceiling check. 2. Vendor text (house style, refine notes, feedback comments, brief) is **data**, sent as labelled JSON fields in the user message, never concatenated into the system prompt. 3. Strict tenant isolation: learning signals of one vendor never reach another vendor's prompts. 4. Every paid call goes through the existing quota, $ cap, kill switch, pilot list and ledger-before-call path. --- ## A. title: Requirement Gaps — Option O (Customer bouquet requests: map pins, vendor offers, accepted order with countdown)
text: # Requirement Gaps — Option O (Customer bouquet requests: map pins, vendor offers, accepted order with countdown) > Companion to REQ-GAPS.md (mobile API, orders, notifications), REQ-GAPS-B.md (customer web app) > and REQ-GAPS-C.md (vendor platform subscription). > Requirement refs point at the tasks in `tasks-ep37-customer-bouquet-requests.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-10-20 > Status: REQ-BRQ-01 … 22 planned (EP-37, see `EPICS-O.md`). ## Context Today the marketplace only goes one way: vendors put bouquets in smart vases and customers buy what is listed (`Order` → `OrderLine` → `BouquetId` + `VaseId`). A customer who wants something specific (a reference photo from Pinterest, "like this but in blue") has no way to ask. This epic adds the reverse flow, a **bouquet request**: ``` Customer: photos + note + budget + when + where ──▶ pin on the vendors' map (approximate location) Vendors in range: offer = price + ready/delivery time + notes (substitutions) + photos Customer: compares offers ──▶ accepts ONE ──▶ others rejected ──▶ pays ──▶ Order at that vendor Order: countdown to the delivery time · phases · "need more time" · late alerts · delivered ``` What exists and what is missing: - `SavedAddress` has street/city/postal code but **no coordinates**. Geocoding already exists (`IGeocodingService` / `IAddressLookupService` in `Infrastructure/Geocoding`: Nominatim, cached, rate-limited, with search and reverse lookup), so the pin reuses it and adds a manual adjustment. - `Order`/`OrderLine` require a `BouquetId` and `VaseId`, so a custom order needs a new line type. - `Notification` is **customer-only** (`CustomerId`) and push is a no-op stub (`NotificationServiceClient`; no FCM client, EP-06 pending). Vendors have no notification inbox (only `VendorMessage`). - SignalR has one hub (`BouquetHub`), customer-facing. - Stripe checkout for orders is fully wired (`StripeService`) and can be reused. **Principles** 1. **Customer privacy first.** Vendors see an approximate location (fuzzed to a ~500 m cell) and district only. The exact address, name and phone are revealed to the chosen vendor after payment, and never to the others. 2. **Requests are vendor-only content.** They never appear on the public/customer map, and a customer sees only their own requests. 3. **One winner, atomically.** Accepting an offer rejects all other offers in the same transaction. 4. **Time is a contract.** Every accepted order has a committed delivery time. Deviations are announced, never silent. --- ## A. Customer creates a request ### REQ-BRQ-01 — Who can request — P0 Only signed-in customers (`CustomerAccess`, realm role `User`) with a **verified email** may create requests. Limits: ≤ 3 open requests per customer, ≤ 10 per rolling 7 days. Suspended customers cannot create them. **Accept**: anonymous → 401; limits → 429 `request-limit` with `Retry-After`. ### REQ-BRQ-02 — Request content — P0 - 1–5 reference images (JPEG/PNG/WebP ≤ 8 MB raw; re-encoded ≤ 1600 px JPEG, EXIF in...

title: Requirement Gaps — Option R (Recognition confidence from human feedback)
text: # Requirement Gaps — Option R (Recognition confidence from human feedback) > Companion to REQ-GAPS-H.md (EP-28 recognition), REQ-GAPS-M.md (EP-33 feedback loop, known corrections) > and REQ-GAPS-N.md (EP-34 stock count, EP-35 bouquet analysis, EP-36 cost assessor). > Requirement refs point at the tasks in `tasks-ep40-recognition-confidence-feedback.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-10-23 > Status: implemented in this repo (EP-40, see `EPICS-R.md`); vendor app EP-M20 pending. Section H decided 2026-10-23 as proposed. ## Context Every recognised line carries a "confidence", shown as "90 % sure" in the Vendor Portal (`_AnalysisReview.cshtml`, the stock count review and the Photos-mode inventory). Today that number is **the model's own guess about itself**. OpenAI returns it as a field in the structured output (`OpenAiBouquetAnalyzer`, schema `confidence: number`). Vision models are badly calibrated at this: almost every line comes back at 0.90–0.95, whether it is right or not. A real bouquet analysis showed spray carnation 90 %, pincushion protea 95 %, astrantia 90 %, astilbe 90 % and eucalyptus 90 %. The "astilbe" was probably partly amaranthus, and the "eucalyptus" was seeded eucalyptus. The number told the florist nothing about which line to check. The goal is a **confidence score that says how often this kind of answer turned out to be right when florists checked it**. It is computed from human feedback, in code, never by the model. ### What the code does today | Area | Behaviour | Where | |---|---|---| | Raw confidence | The model's 0–1 self-rating, clamped and stored on `DetectedItem.Confidence` / `InventoryLine.Confidence` / `StockCountLine.Confidence`. | `BouquetAnalyzers.cs`, `HostedAiProviders.cs`, `DesignAnalysis.Clean` | | Uses of it | `StockMatcher.Score` multiplies the match by `0.7 + 0.3 × confidence` (default 0.75). The stock count flags `NeedsCheck` below 0.6 (`StockCount.CheckBelowConfidence`). | `StockMatcher.cs`, `StockDtos.cs` | | Feedback: Photos mode | When the florist confirms the inventory, `TakeRecognitionDiff` stores Renamed / Recoloured / Recounted / Removed / Added rows (`RecognitionCorrection`). **Lines confirmed unchanged are not stored**, so there is no denominator. | `DesignSessionCommands.cs:296`, `RecognitionCorrection.cs` | | Feedback: bouquet analysis | A row is stored **only** when the florist picks a different stock item. "Not in my stock" and a changed quantity leave no trace. The florist **cannot say "this is not astrantia, it's scabiosa"** on a line with no stock match, and that is exactly the Missing case. | `EditDesignAnalysisItemCommandHandler` | | Feedback: stock count | Reviewed `Counted` movements are written, but recognised-versus-confirmed is not compared. | `StockCountCommands.cs` | | Learning | `RecognitionCorrections.Build` turns renames seen ≥ 2 times into hints for the same vendor's next recognition (EP-33), with no cross-vendor learning. | `RecognitionCorrection.cs`, `DesignJobProcessor.cs:161` |...

title: Requirement Gaps — Option S (Flower atlas, item crops and image matching)
text: # Requirement Gaps — Option S (Flower atlas, item crops and image matching) > Companion to REQ-GAPS-N.md (EP-35 bouquet analysis, EP-36 cost assessor), REQ-GAPS-K.md (EP-31 stock > photos) and REQ-GAPS-R.md (EP-40 recognition confidence from human feedback). > Requirement refs point at the tasks in `tasks-ep41-flower-atlas-image-matching.json`. > Analysis date: 2026-10-23 > Status: Phase 1 + 2 implemented in this repo (EP-41, see `EPICS-S.md`); Phase 3 (REQ-ATL-13/14) and the vendor app > (REQ-ATL-16) pending. Section H decided 2026-10-24 as proposed. ## Context The bouquet analysis review (`_AnalysisReview.cshtml`) shows each detected item as text: a pictogram, a name, colour swatches and a count. The florist can't see **which part of the photo** the AI means, or **what that flower should look like**. Checking a line means scanning the whole photo and remembering what astrantia looks like. Vendors asked for two images per line: 1. **A crop of the item** from their own photo. 2. **A reference image** of the flower the AI named. They also asked whether a **flower atlas compared with real images** could replace parts of the LLM. ### What the code does today | Area | Behaviour | Where | |---|---|---| | Detected items | Kind, name, colours, variety, quantity (+ range), visibility, raw confidence. **No position** in the photo, and no record of which photo it came from. | `DetectedItem` in `DesignAnalysis.cs`, `OpenAiBouquetAnalyzer` | | Analysis photos | 1–5 private photos per session, processed by `SkiaDesignImageProcessor` (re-encoded, EXIF stripped), stored through `IDesignMediaStore` (private R2). | `DesignJobProcessor`, `DesignMediaStores.cs` | | Media serving | `GET /vendor/design-sessions/{id}/media/...` by `DesignMediaKind`; the Vendor Portal proxies it same-origin (`Pages/Design/Media`). | `BouquetDesignController.cs:107`, `Media.cshtml.cs` | | Stock photos | Up to 5 private photos per stock item with a main photo (EP-31). These are labelled, vendor-owned examples of exactly the flowers the shop buys. | `StockPhoto`, `StockAppearanceService` | | Matching | `StockMatcher` compares **text** (canonical name, colour words → ΔE, variety). It never looks at pixels. | `StockMatcher.cs` | | Reference images | None. No flower vocabulary beyond the `StockMatcher` synonym table. | — | ### Approach: combine, don't replace The LLM stays as the item lister. Images are added in three phases. Each phase is useful on its own and decides whether the next one is worth doing. ``` analysis photo(s) ──▶ LLM (or detector) lists items + boxes {photoIndex, x, y, w, h} │ ├─▶ crop (Skia) ─▶ private crop per item ──────────────┐ │ ▼ │ image fingerprint (CLIP/SigLIP/DINOv2) ─▶ nearest neighbours │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ flower atlas entry (by type key) global atlas photos this shop's stock photos │ │ │ └──────────── review line: [crop] [atlas photo] [my stock photo] ───────┘ + "AI says Astilbe, the photo looks like Amaranthus" flag ``` | Phase | Delivers | Effort | |---|---|---| |...
